newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse new split plan seen as positive.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse new split plan seen as positive.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp's modified plan for separating its media and industrial businesses neither surprised nor displeased analysts, who said that grouping Thermo King with the media side could provide more value to the company than keeping it in a lackluster industrial mix.

"After a nanosecond of thought, I wasn't surprised," said Greg Drahuschak at Janney Montgomery Scott. "It gives Westinghouse more time and options regarding what to do with Thermo King. And they'll get a positive contribution from it while adding it to a positive mix."

Westinghouse said Wednesday that in splitting its media and industrial businesses into separate companies later this year, it will group Thermo King, a profitable refrigerated transport unit, with its media operations.
The original plan, announced late in 1996, called for Thermo King to be grouped with Westinghouse's other industrial units: Power Generation, Energy Systems and Government and Environmental Services.

Also under the original plan, Westinghouse was to spin off up to 20 percent of Thermo King and channel the proceeds into the other industrial units, which have been facing sluggish markets and, as a result, sluggish margins.

"It's kind of like having eight baseball players who can't hit the side of a barn and adding Barry Bonds to the mix," Drahuschak said. "You're adding one great element to the mix, but what does it really do in the end for the whole team concept?
Some of the industrial units "have great management, but when the markets stink, that's not under your control," he said.
Westinghouse said that under its new plan, it will consider options for Thermo King to enhance shareholder value, including a sale, public offering or spin-off to shareholders.
It said the new plan will be more beneficial to both its media business, to be called CBS Corp, and its industrial side, to be called Westinghouse Electric Co.

"By retaining Thermo King, we have greater flexibility to apply its strong cash flow to reduce liabilities and also to maintain several attractive options to optimize its value," Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan said in a news release.

Moreover, company spokesman Kevin Ramundo said the industrial company will have positive cash flow and be debt free. Under the original plan, the industrial group would have absorbed $375 million in annual costs to pay pension and post-retirement benefits. These obligations now will be retained by CBS.

"I think (the new plan) makes sense," said Dennis McAlpine at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "The net tax operating loss will be on the broadcast side, and the income generated by Thermo King can be used to pay for that.
"But I don't think Thermo King will be on the broadcast side for very long," he added. "It doesn't make sense. There's obviously no synergy there."
But Drahuschak said CBS Corp management could decide to retain Thermo King indefinitely.

"I could see them doing nothing with it, and no one would be upset by that," he said. "Thermo King will add a positive contribution, and it stands on its own anyway. CBS management won't have to pay much attention to it and fuss and fume over it."
Westinghouse shares were up 5/8 to 22-5/8 in early-afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
